qualifier: Key West's Code of Ordinances sets no minimum or maximum seawall top elevation in any datum. The city's land development rules discourage vertical seawalls altogether: shoreline hardening is allowed only when erosion is a critical peril and vegetation has failed, and riprap comes first. Any wall height is set by your engineer and your permits.
detail_rows: No fixed elevation :: Key West Code Sec. 110-182 (Shoreline vegetation and stability) controls shoreline hardening and states no seawall top elevation in NAVD88, NGVD29 or any other datum. | When hardening is allowed :: Riprap, bulkheads or similar devices are not allowed unless erosion constitutes a critical peril to upland property and vegetation has failed to stabilize the shoreline. Riprap shall be the first alternative. Sec. 110-182(c). | Vertical walls discouraged :: Such shoreline hardening structures shall generally not be vertical seawalls or bulkheads, and pervious interlocking systems, filter mats and similar methods are to be used instead of vertical walls whenever feasible. Sec. 110-182(c) and (c)(2). | Location :: The structure may not sit waterward of the mean high water line unless shown to be in the public interest, and must first be approved by the other public agencies with jurisdiction. Sec. 110-182(c)(3) and (c)(4). | Revegetation :: The design must include a program of shoreline vegetation or revegetation. Sec. 110-182(c)(5). | Permit :: Bulkheads, piers and docks along the shoreline are installed under permit from the building official. Sec. 118-361. | Flood zones :: The floodplain chapter lists bulkheads and seawalls among other development regulated in flood hazard areas. Sec. 34-139.
source: City of Key West Code of Ordinances, Subpart B Land Development Regulations, Sec. 110-182 (Shoreline vegetation and stability); also Sec. 118-361 and Sec. 34-139; online version Aug 21, 2026
notes: Searched Municode full text of the Key West Code of Ordinances and Comprehensive Plan: 'seawall' (8 hits), 'seawalls' (8), 'bulkhead' (10), 'shoreline hardening' (3); 'seawall' in the ordinances tab returned 0. qualifier: Marathon's Land Development Regulations set no minimum or maximum seawall top elevation in any datum. The city fixes a two-foot cap width and a six-inch retention swale, berm or curb behind the wall, but the height comes from your engineer's design and your permits.
detail_rows: No fixed elevation :: Marathon LDR Sec. 106.36(H), Hardened Shorelines, sets the rules for bulkheads and seawalls and states no top elevation in NAVD88, NGVD29 or any other datum. | When a wall is allowed :: Only on residential canals and altered shorelines, and only where riprap or sloping rock revetments with biotechnical erosion control will not suffice, as determined by the City Biologist. Sec. 106.36(H). | Replacement or severe erosion :: Allowed when replacing an existing deteriorated bulkhead or seawall, or to stabilize a severely eroded shoreline where riprap is shown not to be sufficient. Sec. 106.36(H)(1). | Cap width :: Seawalls may have a cap of two feet in width. Sec. 106.36(H)(1). | Retention behind the wall :: The design must include a minimum six-inch retention swale, berm or curb directly landward of the wall. Sec. 106.36(H)(5). | Wall line :: The bulkhead line is set at the property's average mean high water line when the permit is requested, and reclaiming eroded land by bulkheading and backfilling is prohibited. Sec. 106.36(H)(6). | No open water :: No new vertical seawalls or bulkheads on open water shorelines, and none on or waterward of a sea turtle nesting beach. Sec. 106.36(H)(3) and (H)(4). | Engineer required :: All waterfront construction such as docks, piers, seawalls or revetments shall be planned and designed by a professional engineer. Sec. 104.64(B)(16). | V zones :: In coastal high hazard areas, bulkheads and seawalls need other-agency authorization, must stand clear of buildings, and need a design professional's analysis showing no harmful diversion of floodwaters or wave runup. Sec. 107.102.11(E)(1).
source: City of Marathon Code, Appendix A Land Development Regulations, Sec. 106.36(H) Hardened Shorelines; also Secs. 106.38(F), 104.64(B)(16), 107.102.11(E)(1), 108.20(B)

qualifier: Islamorada's Village Code sets no minimum or maximum seawall top elevation in any datum. It is one of the strictest hardening codes in the Keys: vertical seawalls are barred on open water, and a damaged seawall is to be repaired with riprap and native plants unless riprap is shown not to be feasible.
detail_rows: No fixed elevation :: Islamorada Village Code Sec. 30-1545, Bulkheads, seawalls or riprap, sets no seawall top elevation in NAVD88, NGVD29 or any other datum. | Open water :: New vertical seawalls or bulkheads are not permitted on open water except under F.S. 373.414(5). Vertical seawalls as defined in Rule 62-330, F.A.C., shall not be permitted. Sec. 30-1545(a) and (b). | Altered shorelines :: Hardening with bulkheads, seawalls and other vertical structures may be permitted only to stabilize severely eroding shorelines under Rule 62-330.0501(12), F.A.C., and the conditions in subsection (e). Sec. 30-1545(c). | Retention behind the wall :: The design must include a minimum six-inch retention swale, berm or curb directly landward of the system. Sec. 30-1545(b) and (e)(5). | Repairs :: A deteriorated, lawfully existing seawall may be repaired or replaced, keeping the existing footprint to the maximum extent practicable. Damaged seawalls shall be repaired using riprap with native shoreline vegetation, and bulkheads are permitted only if riprap with filter cloth is not feasible. Sec. 30-1545(g). | Cap width :: A seawall may have a cap up to two feet wide without being considered a dock. Sec. 30-1545(i). | Setback :: The shoreline setback does not apply to seawalls, retaining walls, riprap and bulkheads permitted under the division. Sec. 30-1542(c). | V and Coastal A zones :: Bulkheads and seawalls need other-agency authorization, must stand clear of buildings, and need a design professional's analysis showing no harmful diversion of floodwaters or wave runup. Sec. 6-94.4(d)(1).
source: Islamorada, Village of Islands, Village Code Ch. 30 Land Development Regulations, Sec. 30-1545 (Bulkheads, seawalls or riprap); also Sec. 30-1542 and Sec. 6-94.4

qualifier: Key Largo is unincorporated, so Monroe County's Land Development Code governs, and it sets no minimum or maximum seawall top elevation in NAVD88, NGVD29 or any other datum. The only height rule is relative: your yard behind the wall must sit at least six inches below the top of the wall. The design elevation comes from your engineer and your state and federal permits, not from a county number.
detail_rows: No fixed elevation :: Monroe County LDC Sec. 118-12(k), Bulkheads, seawalls, and riprap, sets where and when seawalls are allowed but states no minimum or maximum top elevation in any datum. | The one height rule :: Existing grade landward of the bulkhead shall be at least six inches lower than the top of the bulkhead. Sec. 118-12(k)(2). This is measured against your own yard, not a fixed elevation. | Cap width :: A seawall without a principal use may have a cap no more than two feet wide, and docking attachments such as davits, cleats and platforms are allowed only as accessory to a principal use. Sec. 118-12(k)(1). | Where a vertical wall is allowed :: Only to stabilize a severely eroding shoreline on a manmade canal, channel or basin, and only if native vegetation or riprap with filter cloth is not feasible. No new seawalls, bulkheads or other hardened vertical structures on open water. Sec. 118-12(k)(3). | Repair and replacement :: A lawfully existing, deteriorated seawall may be repaired or replaced and is exempt from the nonsubstantial-improvement limits except on known or potential sea turtle nesting beaches. Keep the existing footprint to the maximum extent practicable. Sec. 118-12(k)(4). | Turtle beaches :: No seawalls, bulkheads or riprap on or waterward of a beach berm that is known or potential marine turtle nesting area. Sec. 118-12(k)(7). | V zones :: In coastal high hazard areas (Zone V), bulkheads and seawalls are allowed only if also authorized by the appropriate federal, state or local authority, located outside and not attached to buildings, and backed by a registered design professional's analysis showing no harmful diversion of floodwaters or wave runup and reflection. Sec. 122-31(d)(1).
source: Monroe County Land Development Code Sec. 118-12(k) (Shoreline Setback - Bulkheads, seawalls, and riprap) and Sec. 122-31(d)(1) (Floodplain Management - Other development); LDC online version May 18, 2026
